section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Analyzing Graphs of Quadratic Functions

title: Find the vertex of f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c (vertex formula)
sources: OpenStax College Algebra 2e §5.1 pp. 395-399 (CC BY 4.0): explanations only, no problems copied
process_card: Finding the vertex with the vertex formula

let.kn: a h^2 + 2 a h^2 + a h^2 + k

steps.name: identify the coefficients (a and b with their signs)
compute the x-coordinate with the vertex formula
write the vertex as a point

mistakes.name: dropped the minus in -b/(2a)
mistakes.message: The formula is x = -b/(2a): if b = 14 and a = -1, then x = -14/(-2) = 7.

hints.step: identify the coefficients (a and b with their signs)
hints.hint: a is the number on x^2, b the number on x, signs included.
hints.why: The vertex formula uses a and b.

hints.step: compute the x-coordinate with the vertex formula
hints.why: Completing the square on ax^2 + bx + c always gives h = -b/(2a).
The vertex is a point on the graph, so its y is f(x).

hints.step: write the vertex as a point
hints.why: The question asks for a point.
